{{nobold|Тристан Вукчевић}} | image = 1 Tristan Vukčević 2025.jpg | image_size = | caption = Vukčević with the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2025 | position = [[Power forward]] | height_ft = 7 | height_in = 0 | weight_lb = 220 | league = [[NBA]] | team = Washington Wizards | number = 00 | nationality = Serbian / Greek / Swedish | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2003|3|11|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Siena]], Italy | draft_year = 2023 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 42 | draft_team = [[Washington Wizards]] | career_start = 2020 | career_end = | years1 = 2019–2022 | team1 = [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] | years2 = 2019–2022 | team2 = →[[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|Real Madrid B]] | years3 = 2022–2024 | team3 = [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] | years4 = {{nbay|2023|end}}–present | team4 = [[Washington Wizards]] | years5 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2026]] | team5 = →[[Capital City Go-Go]] | highlights = * [[ABA League]] champion ([[2022–23 ABA League First Division|2023]]) * [[Supercopa de España de Baloncesto|Spanish Supercup]] winner ([[2021 Supercopa de España de Baloncesto|2021]]) }} '''Tristan Tsalikis Vukčević''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Тристан Цаликис Вукчевић}}, {{langx|el|Τριστάν Τσαλίκης-Βούκτσεβιτς|Tristan Tsalikis-Vouktsevits}}; born 11 March 2003) is a Serbian and Greek professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He also represents the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbian national team]]. ==Early life== Vukčević is the son of Jade (née Čičak) and [[Dušan Vukčević]].{{efn|His father added the name Tsalikis to his family name when he obtained a Greek citizenship.}} He was born in [[Siena]], Italy as his father was playing for [[Mens Sana 1871 Basket|Montepaschi Siena]]. His father is a retired Bosnia-born Serbian professional basketball player who played for [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]], [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], [[Olimpia Milano]], [[Virtus Bologna]] and others during his playing career as well as represented [[Serbia and Montenegro men's national basketball team|Serbia and Montenegro national team]] internationally.{{cite web|title=KRV NIJE VODA: Jedan od najtalentovanijih mladih košarkaša želi da igra za Srbiju! Otac mu je bivši reprezentativac (VIDEO)|url=https://www.kurir.rs/sport/kosarka/3237353/krv-nije-voda-jedan-od-najtalentovanijih-mladih-kosarkasa-zeli-da-igra-za-srbiju-otac-mu-je-bivsi-reprezentativac-video|website=Kurir.rs|date=15 April 2019|access-date=3 September 2020|language=Serbian}} His mother is a Greek-based Swedish businesswoman and former [[swimwear]] model. His mother's parents emigrated to Sweden from the [[former Yugoslavia]].{{cite web|title=About Jade V.|url=https://www.jadevtales.com/about-jade-v/|website=JadeVTales.com|access-date=3 September 2020}} Vukčević holds [[Serbian passport|Serbian]] and [[Greek passport|Greek]] passports through his father, and a [[Swedish passport]] through his mother.{{cite web|title=Enigma Tristan Vukčević|url=https://kosmagazin.com/enigma-tristan-vukcevic/|website=KosMagazin.com|date=20 January 2020|access-date=3 September 2020|language=Serbian}} Vukčević grew up in Italy, where his father played professionally. Following Dušan's retirement, the family moved back to [[Athens]], Greece. He started to play basketball for the [[youth system]] of his father's former club, Olympiacos. In 2018, Vukčević joined the U16 team of Spanish club Real Madrid,{{cite web|title=Ala-pívot Tristan|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/baloncesto/cantera/cadete-a/tristan-vukcevic|website=RealMadrid.com|access-date=3 September 2020}} another father's former club. Vukčević won the [[2019–20 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament#Munich, Germany|Munich Tournament]] for the [[2019–20 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|2019–20 Euroleague NGT]] season with U18 Real Madrid. Over four tournament games, he averaged 16 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game.{{cite web|title=TSALIKIS, TRISTAN U18 Real Madrid|url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=009212&seasoncode=JTM19#!JTM19_QLF|website=AdidasNGT.com|access-date=3 September 2020}} Afterward, the Final Tournament was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe|COVID-19 pandemic]]. ==Professional career== ===Real Madrid (2019–2022)=== On 2 September 2020, Vukčević made his pre-season debut for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in a 68–66 win over [[Real Betis Baloncesto|Coosur Real Betis]] recording 8 points.{{cite web|title=Tristan Vukcevic steals the show in debut with Real Madrid's senior team|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1096399/tristan-vukcevic-steals-the-show-in-debut-with-real-madrids-senior-team/|website=EuroHoops.net|date=2 September 2020|access-date=3 September 2020}}{{cite web|title=68–66: Segunda victoria de la pretemporada|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/noticias/2020/09/02/68-66-segunda-victoria-de-la-pretemporada|website=RealMadrid.com|date=2 September 2020|access-date=3 September 2020|language=Spanish}} On 11 October, he made his professional debut in a 90–65 win over [[CB Gran Canaria|Herbalife Gran Canaria]] recording 2 points and 2 rebounds in 4 minutes.{{cite web|title=October 2020, Herbalife GC 65–90 Real Madrid|url=https://www.acb.com/partido/estadisticas/id/101280|website=ACB.com|access-date=12 October 2020}} ===Partizan Belgrade (2022–2024)=== On 27 January 2022, Vukčević signed a multi-year contract with [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] of the [[ABA League]].{{cite web|title=Tristan Vukčević potpisao za Partizan|url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2022&mm=01&dd=27&nav_id=2095857|website=b92.net|date=27 January 2022|access-date=27 January 2022|language=Serbian}}{{cite web|title=Tristan Vukčević pens multi-year contract with Partizan NIS|url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news/46315/tristan-vukcevic-pens-multi-year-contract-with-partizan-nis/|website=ABA-Liga.com|date=27 January 2022|access-date=27 January 2022}} In 2022–23 season, he won the [[2022–23 ABA League First Division|ABA League]] championship title with Partizan. Over 22 ABA League games, he averaged 8.1 points and 3.2 rebounds on 58% shooting from the field. In the EuroLeague, he had a more limited role within the team.{{citation needed|date=August 2025}} During the 2023–24 season, Vukčević averaged 4.2 points and 2.3 rebounds over 12 EuroLeague games. In [[2023–24 ABA League First Division|ABA League]], he appeared in 14 games, averaging 10.9 points and 3.6 rebounds on 54.4% shooting from the field.{{citation needed|date=August 2025}} On 13 March 2024, Vukčević parted ways with Partizan Belgrade to pursue his NBA career.{{cite news|title=Tristan Vukčević više nije košarkaš Partizana|url=https://www.politika.rs/sr/clanak/603948/Sport/Kosarka/Tristan-Vukcevic-vise-nije-kosarkas-Partizana|website=Politika.rs|date=13 March 2024|access-date=13 March 2024|language=Serbian}} During his three seasons at the club, Vukčević played 75 games and scored 453 points along with 198 rebounds and 48 assists.{{citation needed|date=August 2025}} ===Washington Wizards / Capital City Go-Go (2024–present)=== Vukčević had a strong showing at the 2023 [[NBA draft combine]], scoring 21 points in 17 minutes in the lone game he played.{{cite web|first=Colin|last=Gallant|title=Tristan Vukcevic will remain in 2023 NBA Draft after Combine standout|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba-draft-news-combine-standout-makes-final-decision-tristan-vukcevic|website=ClutchPoints.com|date=12 June 2023|access-date=23 June 2023}} He was subsequently selected with the 42nd overall pick by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=2023 NBA Draft Results: Picks 1-58|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-nba-draft-order|website=NBA.com|access-date=23 June 2023}} On 14 March 2024, Vukčević signed with the Wizards.{{cite web|title=Wizards Sign Vukcevic|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-vukcevic|website=NBA.com|date=14 March 2024|access-date=14 March 2024}} He managed to play in 10 NBA regular-season games until the end of the season, averaging 8.5 points and 3.6 rebounds per game. On 3 July, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with Washington.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Wizards Re-Sign Tristan Vukcevic To Two-Way Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/wizards-re-sign-tristan-vukcevic-to-two-way-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=3 July 2024|access-date=3 July 2024}}{{cite web|title=Wizards Sign Vukcevic to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-vukcevic-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=3 July 2024|access-date=3 July 2024}} Vukčević made 35 appearances (one start) for the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 9.4 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.1 assists. On 10 July 2025, Vukčević re-signed with Washington on another two-way contract.{{cite web | last=Brown | first=Henry | title=Wizards Re-Sign Tristan Vukcevic | website=Washington Wizards On SI | date=2025-07-10 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/wizards/onsi/washington-wizards-news/washington-wizards-re-sign-tristan-vukcevic | access-date=2025-12-01}} On 21 February 2026, the Wizards signed Vukčević to a three-year, $9 million standard contract.{{Cite web|title=Washington Signs Tristan Vukčević to Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/washington-signs-tristan-vukcevic-to-multi-year-contract|access-date=February 23, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} ==National team career== Due to his father's background, Vukčević is eligible to represent [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greece]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina men's national basketball team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]], or [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia]] internationally, while due to his mother's background he is eligible to represent [[Sweden men's national basketball team|Sweden]]. Also, he is eligible to represent [[Italy men's national basketball team|Italy]] or [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain]].{{cite web|title=MAJKA ŠVEĐANKA, OTAC SA GRČKIM DRŽAVLJANSTVOM!
